source_evidence.observation: The proposition binds an arbitrary random variable X and positive parameters K_i. Property (c) is E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K_3 lambda), expressly for 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3.
The exercise asks the reader to argue that the bound in property (c) cannot be extended to all lambda satisfying |lambda| <= 1/K_3.

binders: A random variable X (inherited from Proposition 2.7.1; PDF page 21, printed page 32).
A positive parameter K_3 from property (c) (Proposition 2.7.1 heading and property (c); PDF page 21, printed page 32).
A real MGF parameter lambda in the contemplated symmetric interval |lambda| <= 1/K_3 (Exercise 2.7.4; PDF page 22, printed page 33).
hypotheses: The original property-(c) setting uses E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K_3 lambda) on the one-sided interval 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3 (PDF page 21, printed page 32).
K_3 > 0, as stipulated for the parameters K_i in Proposition 2.7.1 (PDF page 21, printed page 32).
conclusions: The property-(c) bound cannot, in general, be required for every real lambda with |lambda| <= 1/K_3; the proposed addition of negative lambda is invalid (Exercise 2.7.4, PDF page 22, printed page 33, read with property (c) on PDF page 21, printed page 32).
definitions_and_conventions: MGF means expectation of an exponential; here the exact expression is E exp(lambda |X|), retaining the absolute value around X (property (c), PDF page 21, printed page 32).
The right-hand side of the bound is exp(K_3 lambda), linear in lambda in the exponent (property (c), PDF page 21, printed page 32).

The original interval 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3 and the proposed interval |lambda| <= 1/K_3 are distinct: only the latter includes negative lambda (property (c), PDF page 21, printed page 32; Exercise 2.7.4, PDF page 22, printed page 33).
implicit_context: The exercise occurs immediately after Proposition 2.7.1 and refers back to that proposition's property (c) rather than introducing a new MGF formula (PDF pages 21-22, printed pages 32-33).

The claim is a general impossibility of the proposed strengthening, so an argument exhibiting failure for an admissible random variable is sufficient; the source does not prescribe a particular witness (Exercise 2.7.4, PDF page 22, printed page 33).

details: Property (c) quantifies only over 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3 (PDF page 21, printed page 32).
Exercise 2.7.4 tests the stronger quantification over all lambda with |lambda| <= 1/K_3, thereby adding negative lambda (PDF page 22, printed page 33).
The tested inequality remains E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K_3 lambda); it is not the centered-variable quadratic MGF bound of property (e) (property (c), PDF page 21, printed page 32).
The exercise asks for an argument that the symmetric extension is unavailable in general, rather than asserting failure for every individual X and K_3 (Exercise 2.7.4, PDF page 22, printed page 33).

undebatable_constraints: The original property (c) interval is 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3, not |lambda| <= 1/K_3 (PDF page 21, printed page 32).
The rejected extension is specifically to every lambda satisfying |lambda| <= 1/K_3, which introduces negative lambda (Exercise 2.7.4, PDF page 22, printed page 33).
The expression under discussion is E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K_3 lambda), with |X| inside the exponential and a linear K_3 lambda exponent on the right (property (c), PDF page 21, printed page 32).
K_3 is positive (Proposition 2.7.1 heading, PDF page 21, printed page 32).

The exercise requests a general counterargument to the proposed extension; it must not silently replace property (c) by the distinct, symmetric property-(e) bound for a centered X (PDF pages 21-22, printed pages 32-33).

ambiguities.issue: The exercise does not specify the form of the counterargument or a particular counterexample.
ambiguities.evidence: Exercise 2.7.4 says only 'Argue that' the extension cannot be made (PDF page 22, printed page 33).
ambiguities.impact: A faithful solution may use any valid admissible witness or a more general obstruction; the source contract should not require one particular witness.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase 'cannot be extended' is not explicitly formalized with existential and universal quantifiers in the prose.
ambiguities.evidence: Exercise 2.7.4 refers tersely to 'the bound in property c' and the proposed symmetric lambda range (PDF page 22, printed page 33).
ambiguities.impact: In context it rejects a general strengthening of property (c), not the stronger and generally false assertion that every random variable fails the two-sided bound for every positive K_3.

contracts.contract_plain_english: For an arbitrary random variable, Proposition 2.7.1(c) gives the MGF-of-absolute-value inequality E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K_3 lambda) only for nonnegative lambda between 0 and 1/K_3. Exercise 2.7.4 asks for an argument that this same bound is not valid as a general replacement on the symmetric interval |lambda| <= 1/K_3, because that would additionally require it at negative lambda. The exercise leaves the particular counterargument open.
